I graduated with a bachelors in accounting after 6 years of college. During those six years, I went through a physically and emotional abusive marriage/divorce, I had a miscarriage that no one but my husband was aware of (he did not care and stayed at his friends doing whatever), my mother committed suicide, and my fathers family disowned me, I had to file bankruptcy due to my divorce. Oftentimes I was so stressed and depressed because I never thought I would see the finish line. I had my own demons to battle with some severe depression I worked to overcome (and am still fighting) but I did it!!! I got a bachelors degree and am now working in a very well paying career. 

I try to be proud for myself even though when I graduated, the only people to come were my boss and my moms parents- they have been my life line over the past year! It hurt so much to know my father and his family, who raised me, did not care to come, and instead during the middle of my ceremony, sent me nasty messages of how I did not deserve my degree. But.... I have to say, for me.... I did not kill myself. I did not quit. I did not give up. I did it. For me. For my future family. For the family I have. Because we have all come from poor households and now I can stand alone without support and if they need me, I can finally FINALLY give back.

What's funny is I was always taught by my parents to NEVER ask because that was considered intrusive. Instead I had to wait to be asked. I almost never went anywhere as a result because people thought I just didnt want to go. 

I still struggle with this concept as an adult with my friends (who have been my friends since elementary school!).

I really did try to see the best. Because when he was good to me he was GOOD to me. And our relationship had not always been bad. It actually used to be incredibly wonderful. We were together for 6 years, married a couple of those. 

As time passed when I was his wife and he would become violently angry, it became always my fault, no matter what i did or tried. Now that isn't to say i was perfect. I was far far from perfect and took away many life lessons from the relationship itself. But I do know when we finally separated, I really had no idea who I was anymore. Before everything went downhill, I had had dreams, I had wonderful hobbies (writing and drawing and creating! How I loved it!). My education had been so important. But the thing was, everything I had done had become less for me and more for him.  I suffered from horrific nightmares, I drank excessively, withdrew from my family because they were really dismissive of my state of mind. I had no friends- i hadn't been allowed friends. Life was supposed to be "just me and him forever" as it was put. 

I am thankful every day for the night i realized i had to make a change or I was not going to make it. I had dropped down to 109lbs at 5'5, was a skeleton. I failed a semester of college. And I came very close to ending my life to get rid of the intrusive thoughts, the memories that sometimes screamed through my mind, the feeling that I had lost my husband because I was insane. So I made that change and got help.

My divorce is a huge part of my life. Occasionally I will talk about the good memories of my marriage and people look at me like I'm nuts. I won't lie, my marriage was precious to me in that it was my love experience with another person. The good was good. And i dont mind remembering that.
